summary: The diff is additive (new YAML article, a documented bashrc snippet, and a test script) and does not touch .github/workflows/** or any tier2-triggering path, so tier1 classification is correct, but the guard mechanism itself does not deliver the 'real, technical, non-bypassable enforcement' it claims: the block is gated entirely on whether the plain environment variable INVOCATION_ID is unset, which any interactive session (including the AI session this is meant to constrain) can trivially spoof with a one-line 'export INVOCATION_ID=x' before running gh pr merge or git push, fully defeating the guard with no privilege required; the shipped test suite actually demonstrates this exact bypass path (labeled 'systemd-simulated') without recognizing it as a spoofable escape hatch available to the same actor the control is meant to stop. Additional undisclosed gaps: the shell-function wrapper is bypassable via 'command git ...', the real binary's full path, or 'unset -f git'/'unset -f gh'; 'gh api ... /pulls/N/merge' achieves the same merge effect while evading the 'pr merge'-specific check; and 'git push --all' from a non-protected current branch can still push master/main because the fallback destination logic only inspects the current branch. None of these are mentioned in the snippet's own 'known_limitation' section, which discusses only the Owner-vs-AI ambiguity and not these more basic bypasses. Because the task's explicit goal was real enforcement rather than another paper rule, and the PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml entry asserts this is genuine technical enforcement other sessions will rely on, this should go back for rework (e.g., a check that can't be forged by an ordinary env var, and closing the command/api/path bypasses) rather than be merged as-is.
issues: INVOCATION_ID gate is a plain environment variable check with no cryptographic/systemd-verified binding -- any interactive session can bypass the entire guard with 'export INVOCATION_ID=x' before running the blocked command; this is not meaningfully different from the 'written text' rule the task claims to replace, and it is undisclosed in known_limitation.

Shell-function wrapper is trivially bypassed via 'command git push ...'/'command gh pr merge ...', invoking the real binary by full path, or 'unset -f git'/'unset -f gh' in the same shell -- none of these are covered by the test suite or disclosed as limitations.

'gh api -X PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N/merge' (or other non-'pr merge' gh subcommands that achieve a merge) is not intercepted, since the guard only pattern-matches on argv[1]=='pr' && argv[2]=='merge'.

'git push --all' (or --mirror) run from a non-protected current branch is not blocked even though it can still push master/main, because the destination-resolution fallback only inspects the current branch via 'git symbolic-ref --short HEAD'.
